newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia budget awaits likely upper house approval.
newsitem.headline: Russia budget awaits likely upper house approval.

text.p: The upper chamber of the Russian parliament debates the 1997 budget on Wednesday and a senior official said the document was likely to pass.
"The budget vote will be diffcult but it will pass," Konstantin Titov, head of the Federation Council's budget committee, told reporters.
Finance Minister Alexander Livshits appealed to deputies to vote for the budget, describing the plan as a realistic one which could not be radically improved.
"The discussion so far has been constructive, and there is understanding in the chamber," he said.
"On behalf of the government I ask you to support the budget. It will be difficult to fulfil it, but the past six months of work have shown that it is impossible to improve the plan radically."
Livshits said the budget would help keep inflation from rising, reduce yields on government securities and promote economic growth.
Industrial output crept 0.3 percent above year-ago levels last month and gross domestic product rose a meagre 0.1 percent.
The draft envisages a deficit of 3.5 percent of gross domestic product, by Russian calculations, on revenues of 434.4 trillion roubles ($76.8 billion) and expenditure of 529.8 trillion roubles.
Budget approval is crucial for Russia, seeking to get regular tranches of a $10 billion loan from the International Monetary Fund.
The IMF, angered by abysmal tax revenues in 1996, withheld two tranches of its latest credit in the final quarter of last year, although it relented as tax money started flowing in.
Last week it decided to hand over almost $650 million of its three-year loan to Russia.
The State Duma lower house of parliament approved the draft at a fourth and final reading on January 24. If the Federation Council approves it, it must be signed into law by President Boris Yeltsin.

Livshits said the budget could use on some additional revenues, including from changes in tax legislation. These will produce an additional 40 trillion roubles, inlcuding some 20 trillion roubles from the taxation of government securities.
New arrangements for excise on oil and gas and tougher controls of alcohol production would bring in another 10.7 trillion roubles, he said. ($ = 5653 Russian Roubles)
